title: Penile Erectile Tissue Anatomy: Corpora, Fascia & Nerve
description: Learn penile erectile tissue anatomy in cross-section and length, comparing paired corpora cavernosa, urethra-bearing corpus spongiosum, and deep arteries.
h1: Penile Erectile Tissue Anatomy: Corpora Cavernosa, Spongiosum and Vessels
blurb: Three cylindrical vascular columns—paired dorsal corpora cavernosa and the ventral urethra-bearing corpus spongiosum—wrapped in tough tunica albuginea and Buck fascia.
lead: In cross-section, the shaft of the penis is built around three cylindrical columns of vascular sinusoidal tissue wrapped in tough collagenous sleeves. In this illustrated guide to penile erectile tissue anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including paired corpora cavernosa, corpus spongiosum, tunica albuginea, cavernosal trabeculae—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: In cross-section, the shaft of the penis is built around three cylindrical columns of vascular sinusoidal tissue wrapped in tough collagenous sleeves. The paired corpora cavernosa are enveloped by strong tunica albuginea and form the main rigid erectile compartment; the ventral corpus spongiosum surrounds the penile urethra and expands distally as the glans. Deep penile arteries feed cavernous spaces. Parasympathetic-associated cavernous neural signaling relaxes smooth muscle, increasing arterial inflow and restricting subtunical venous outflow. The spongiosum remains comparatively compliant to protect urethral patency. Within the human body, the penile erectile tissue (Corpora cavernosa · corpus spongiosum) is situated in root, shaft and glans of penis; superficial perineal pouch to external genitalia, receives arterial perfusion via internal pudendal → deep, dorsal and bulbourethral/urethral arteries, and is innervated by dorsal penile nerve (pudendal S2–S4); cavernous nerves from pelvic plexus.

The paired corpora cavernosa (Corpora cavernosa penis) is two dorsal longitudinal erectile cylinders that unite in shaft and separate proximally as crura. Physiologically, the paired corpora cavernosa governs primary rigid erectile compartment. The corpus spongiosum (Corpus spongiosum penis) is single ventral erectile column surrounding spongy urethra. Physiologically, the corpus spongiosum governs engorges without compressing urethral lumen closed. Structurally, the tunica albuginea comprises strong fibrous sheath encasing cavernosa, with distinct collagen layers. Physiologically, the tunica albuginea governs resists expansion and aids venous occlusion. Structurally, the cavernosal trabeculae (Trabeculae corporum cavernosorum) comprises smooth-muscle and connective-tissue struts bordering interconnected blood sinusoids. Physiologically, the cavernosal trabeculae governs relaxation permits filling of cavernous lacunae. Structurally, the deep penile arteries (Arteriae profundae penis) comprises internal pudendal branches traveling within each corpus cavernosum. Physiologically, the deep penile arteries governs feed cavernosal tissue. The helicine arteries (Arteriae helicinae) are small coiled branches entering cavernous sinusoidal spaces. Physiologically, the helicine arteries governs dilate as smooth muscle relaxes, increasing inflow.

Clinically, regarding the paired corpora cavernosa, fibrous tunica helps compress emissary venous outflow. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the corpus spongiosum, its distal expansion is the glans penis. In clinical pathology involving the tunica albuginea, disruption during trauma can constitute penile fracture. Medical evaluation of the cavernosal trabeculae also notes that vascular dysfunction can impair rigidity.

questions.question: What are the three erectile bodies of the penis?
questions.answer: Two paired corpora cavernosa form the main dorsal erectile cylinders. A single corpus spongiosum surrounds the urethra and expands into the glans. The paired corpora cavernosa (Corpora cavernosa penis) is two dorsal longitudinal erectile cylinders that unite in shaft and separate proximally as crura. Physiologically, the paired corpora cavernosa governs primary rigid erectile compartment.

questions.question: What does the tunica albuginea do in erectile tissue?
questions.answer: It is a dense connective-tissue covering around erectile compartments, particularly strong around the corpora cavernosa. Structurally, the tunica albuginea comprises strong fibrous sheath encasing cavernosa, with distinct collagen layers. Physiologically, the tunica albuginea governs resists expansion and aids venous occlusion.

questions.question: What are the paired corpora cavernosa?
questions.answer: Two dorsal longitudinal erectile cylinders that unite in shaft and separate proximally as crura. Functionally, it governs primary rigid erectile compartment. The cavernosal septum is fibrous partition between right and left corpora cavernosa, incomplete distally in places. Physiologically, the cavernosal septum connects paired erectile bodies.

questions.question: Where is the tunica albuginea located?
questions.answer: Strong fibrous sheath encasing cavernosa, with distinct collagen layers. Functionally, it governs resists expansion and aids venous occlusion. Structurally, the glans penis comprises distal expansion of corpus spongiosum over tips of corpora cavernosa. Physiologically, the glans penis contains terminal urethral opening and sensory receptors.

questions.question: What is the function of the deep penile arteries?
questions.answer: Functionally, it governs feed cavernosal tissue. Internal pudendal branches traveling within each corpus cavernosum.
